claims.text: Increasing short-range order in BCC refractory multi-component alloys increases yield strength.
Increasing short-range order in BCC refractory multi-component alloys may reduce ductility.
TaNbHfZrTi can form a BCC refractory multi-component alloy with a nominally random solid-solution state.
Slow cooling promotes short-range order in the proposed alloy.
Rapid quenching preserves a comparatively disordered, low-SRO state in the proposed alloy.
The degree of short-range order can be assessed through diffuse scattering or electron-diffraction patterns.
Enhanced short-range order creates local chemical environments that impede dislocation glide.
Enhanced short-range order impedes dislocation nucleation.
Impeded dislocation motion produces higher yield strength.
Limiting dislocation motion reduces plasticity and ductility.
At approximately 25 °C and a strain rate near 10^-3 s^-1, the SRO-enhanced alloy is expected to have higher yield strength than the quenched baseline.
At approximately 25 °C and a strain rate near 10^-3 s^-1, the SRO-enhanced alloy is expected to have lower ductility than the quenched baseline.
The proposed relationship applies to refractory BCC multi-component alloys such as TaNbHfZrTi within the tested composition and processing range.
The influence of short-range order may differ at temperatures or strain rates far outside the proposed test conditions.
The strengthening contribution attributable solely to short-range order may be subtle and masked by other microstructural features.
Measured short-range order may not fully explain variations in mechanical behavior.
